Foreign purchases of US equities are up to a record ~$850 billion over the last 12 months.

BREAKING: Gulf nations have issued $112 billion in bonds year-to-date, the highest amount on record for this point of the year.

Bond sales have more than tripled since 2022.

This comes as Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE, and Qatar seek financing for infrastructure that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.

This includes new ports on the Red Sea and the Gulf of Oman, repairing older oil and gas pipelines, and improving road networks across these countries.

Kuwait alone raised $6.0 billion last week, with investor orders reaching $14.8 billion, more than double the amount issued, highlighting resilient demand for the debt of Gulf nations.

Gulf nations are borrowing at a record pace as they rush to reshape their infrastructure.

Japan spent a record $74 billion to prop up the yen. It still hit a 40-year low.

The yen funds the world's carry trade. Big money borrows it near zero and buys higher-yielding assets everywhere else. In August 2024 a sharp yen rally forced that trade to unwind and global stocks fell fast.

Japan holds $1.09 trillion in reserves and defends a line near 160 per dollar. A yen that snaps back is how global risk-off starts. Watch 160.

tweets.text: On this day in 1775, the Second Continental Congress established the American postal system and named Benjamin Franklin the first Postmaster General, nearly a year before the colonies declared independence. A reliable mail network was not a convenience but a weapon: it let Congress coordinate the rebellion, move intelligence, and bind 13 colonies into something that could act as one. Franklin, who had already spent 2 decades reforming the colonial post under the British, cut delivery times between major cities and put the system on a formal footing, surveying routes and setting rates. The institution he built became the communications backbone of American commerce for 2 centuries, carrying contracts, payments, and newspapers to every corner of the country. The U.S. Postal Service now delivers nearly half of the world's mail, more than 100 billion pieces a year.

Franklin, who had already spent 2 decades reforming the colonial post under the British, cut delivery times between major cities and put the system on a formal footing, surveying routes and setting rates. The institution he built became the communications backbone of American commerce for 2 centuries, carrying contracts, payments, and newspapers to every corner of the country. The U.S. Postal Service now delivers nearly half of the world's mail, more than 100 billion pieces a year.
